Case reference: 2014002108.CaseDesc: On August 18, 1978, Craig Waldum took part in a canoeing expedition along the Nelson River in Gillam, Manitoba, with seven other people. The remaining five members, including Craig, were in the second canoe. While guiding the canoe to shore, they gave the rope some slack. This caused the bow of the canoe to turn out into the current and tip over. Those on the shore were unable to hold onto the rope because of the strength of the current and the canoe was swept downstream. Craig held onto the canoe for a couple of hours, and then he was seen to let go. He slipped under the water and did not resurface. His remains have not been recovered.

The pilot was advised to turn west, then Air Traffic Control lost radio and radar contact with the plane. Debris from the plane was located on August 27, 1986 in Lake Erie, approximately 32 nautical miles south of the St.Thomas Airport. Debris was drifting in a southeast direction and was recovered approximately 1-3 nautical miles on the Canadian side of the international boundary line in Lake Erie. Debris was identified by Bud Field,  brother of Terry Field, as having come from the missing aircraft.

Case reference: 2014004796.CaseDesc: Shirley Lee Cletheroe was last seen on June 9, 2006 in the Fort St. John area. She has had no contact with her friends or family since that date.

Case reference: 2014002270.CaseDesc: On 2 July, 1992, Behnam Amjadi was seen for the last time when he left his residence in the Côtes-des-Neiges et Notre-Dame-de-Grace district in Montreal, Quebec. Behnam has not been seen and has not contacted his ex-spouse or his brothers in Iran since.

Case reference: 2014005084.CaseDesc: On February 1, 2008, it is suspected Kevin Leroux went through the ice on his ATV, near St Joseph's Cove, Newfoundland and Labrador. Kevin's ATV was recovered several months later, about 22 km from where he was suspected of going through the ice but his body was never found.

Case reference: 2014006282.CaseDesc: On November 26, 2012, a relative of Jean-Marc Lavallée called the Roussillon inter-municipal police to check on Jean-Marc at his residence in La Prairie, Québec. The police found that Jean-Marc was not at his residence and his vehicle was not in the parking lot. The police took numerous steps to locate Jean-Marc, but he remains missing and was seen for the last time on November 25, 2012.

Case reference: 2014002857.CaseDesc: Colin Campbell was last seen March 12, 1998 in Saint John, New Brunswick. Colin was seen jumping off the Reversing Falls Bridge. His body has not been recovered.
